faq.a: Asadullah is associated with the Arabic form أَسَدُ اللَّه, whose core sense is asadullah; lion of god.

faq.q: What is the origin of Asadullah?
faq.a: Asadullah is associated with Arabic. Asadullah is Arabic أَسَدُ اللَّه (Asad Allāh), meaning 'lion of God'.
Yes — the underlying form أَسَدُ اللَّه is Arabic.
Asadullah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Asadullah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Asad Allāh is a compound of Arabic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Asadullah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Asadullah is rendered اسد اللہ and carries the sense اسد اللہ، اللہ کا شیر.

faq.q: What does Asadullah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Asadullah is rendered اسدالله and carries the sense اسدالله، شیر خدا.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-sa-dul-lah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Asadullah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Asadullah, asadullah. Script forms are أَسَدُ اللَّه, اسد الله, اسد اللہ, اسدالله, असदुल्लाह.

faq.q: Is Asadullah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
